newsitem.title: UK: From the flightdeck - The Air Cargo Week in Review.
newsitem.headline: From the flightdeck - The Air Cargo Week in Review.

text.p: This is Reuters' look back at the major developments in the global air cargo industry in the week September 9 - September 13.
**SEPTEMBER 9**

HAMILTON - Kiwi International Airlines chief executive Ewan Wilson says it collapsed with the loss of more than 250 jobs, after a young New Zealand businessman failed in a David and Goliath battle with Australasia's most powerful airlines.

SYDNEY - Qantas Airways says it would offer special fares to passengers stranded in New Zealand and Australia after budget airline Kiwi International Airlines said earlier it would go into voluntary liquidation.
COPENHAGEN - SAS says it inaugurated a new non-stop, three times weekly, scheduled route between Stockholm and Arkangelsk, north Russia.
LONDON - British Midland Airways says it has introduced a series of product improvements including business class to its domestic UK services.
MOSCOW - Transaero says it has announced discounts on all of its flights in the former Soviet Union from September 15.

FRANKFURT - German white collar union DAG says wage talks at Lufthansa started with wide differences of opinion between the airlines and its main unions, both of which have already rejected the airline's call for a pay freeze.
BOMBAY - McDonnell Douglas says it planned to use aircraft equipment from India in the building of its MD-80 and MD-90 models.
GENEVA - ACI says freight and mail traffic handled by 460 airports around the world in May 1996 totalled 4.09 million tonnes, up 7.5 percent on the same month last year.
* ACI says world airports reported a rise in May of six per cent in passenger traffic and eight percent in cargo over the same month last year.

MADRID - Iberia chairman Xavier de Irala says it made a net profit of 4.8 billion pesetas in July, taking its net result for the first seven months of the year into black figures for the first time in many years.
* A company spokesman says Prima Air, a Spanish independent airline, that started operation in March this year, is expecting to take delivery of a third aircraft in the next few months.
Northwest Airlines president John Dasburg says it will increase non-stop services from Minneapolis/St Paul to Tokyo to a daily schedule from four times weekly, effective December 1.

ROME - Virgin Express chief executive Jonathan Orstein says it will complain to the EC over new tariffs introduced by SAS, which has cut the cost of tickets on its Brussels-Copenhagen route but only for those flights which directly coincided with the cheap Virgin flights.
* Ornstein also says it expects to build its fleet around aircraft supplied by U.S. manufacturer Boeing.
* Richard Branson, owner of Virgin Express, says it is making a profit less than half a year after taking off and it expects to revolutionise European air travel by enabling more people to fly.
MILWAUKEE - Midwest Holdings says Midwest Express Airlines named Christopher White director of safety and regulatory compliance.
NEW YORK - InVision Technologies says Israel's El Al airline has ordered a new $1 million bomb detection system for use at New York's John Kennedy international airport.
* Tower Air says that Ramesh Punwani has joined the company as chief financial officer.
KANSAS CITY - Vanguard Airlines says it will begin daily non-stop services between Dallas/Fort Worth and Phoenix on October 1.
**SEPTEMBER 10**
JAKARTA - The Jakarta Post newspaper says Indonesia is to limit arrivals of foreign cargo aircraft to Hang Nadim airport on Batam Island, in an effort to protect domestic cargo carriers.
MANILA - Philippine Airlines' company official says shareholders voted to double the carrier's authorised capital to 10 billion pesos from the current 5.0 billion pesos.

STOCKHOLM - SAS director of European affairs, Hans Ollongren says it rejected Virgin's complaint that SAS was undercutting prices on the Brussels-Copenhagen route, accusing Virgin of fearing competition.
LONDON - Air Action says it has appointed Zena Jones as general manager of international mail direct.
GENEVA - ACI says Memphis was the world's busiest cargo airport in the period January to May 1996.
* ACI says freight and mail traffic handled by 460 airports between January and May 1996, totalled 19,43 million tonnes, up 4.1 percent on the same period the previous year.
* ACI says Memphis was the world's busiest cargo airport in May 1996.
NEW DELHI - The Press Trust of India news agency says Indian Civil Aviation Minister C M Ibrahim says the government will not allow foreigners to take stakes in state-run Indian Airlines.
LONDON - McDonnell Douglas Corp says the cargo version of its C17 military transporter had been received with much interest from potential customers.
BRUSSELS - Richard Branson says he was not aiming to lodge a formal complaint against SAS which he said is flouting European competition rules.
* Richard Branson says he would welcome the development of "Super Jumbo" jets and would order them for his Virgin Atlantic Airways airline.
* Richard Branson says he expected his cut-price regional airline Virgin Express to more than double the number of its planes by the turn of the century.
* Richard Branson says he was not ruling our a closer "relationship" with another airline.
* Richard Branson says he knew competition for his fledgling Virgin Express low-cost regional airline would be weak.
MOSCOW - Aeroflot senior official says it wants to improve the efficiency of its use of a hub at Ireland's Shannon airport.
PRAGUE - The U.S. and Czech Republic says it will sign an air transport agreement which Washington is calling a model "open skies" deal with a former Communist state.
ISTANBUL - Turkish Airlines says it is to co-operate with Air France Cargo to run scheduled cargo flights from Turkey to North America.
ATLANTA - Delta Airlines says it expects stronger than previously anticipated growth in September revenues, more than offsetting cost increases.
FRANKFURT - Air India cargo sale manager Ruedger Brasche says it has cancelled its four-time weekly Brussels to India freighter service due to high losses.
* Air India says it will start twice-weekly Mumbai to Chicago service with a Frankfurt stopover from October 31.
* Air India cargo sales manager Germany Ruediger Brasche says it will keep official ex-Germany air cargo rates stable this autumn but it will try to raise ad-hoc prices.
KUWAIT - The civil aviation authority says Kuwait International airport handled six percent more cargo and four percent more passengers in August 1996, compared to the same month last year.
DUBAI - Iranian Asseman Airlines spokesman says it and Kyrgyzstan Airlines launched a joint-weekly service between the countries' capitals.
MOSCOW - Aeroflot International airlines deputy chief executive Valery Okulov says it plans to buy 10 Boeing 737-400 passenger jets in 1997-1998, paying for them over an extended period.
ROME - A Genoa airport spokesman says Genoa Cristoforo Colombo airport has seen cargo traffic increase by 3.7 percent to 2.8 million kg, for the first seven months of the year.
COPENHAGEN - Virgin Express says that it might lease its cargo capacity to a specialist operator.
LONDON - The Italian Association of International Air Couriers says in a statement it named Renato Carrara as chairman.
HAMBURG - Germany's federal aviation office says it had banned Turkish charter airline Holiday Air from landing in Germany because its aircraft had been found to be unsafe.
LAS PALMAS - Airport figures show cargo traffic at Spain's Gran Canaria airport fell 6.8 percent in August to 2,003 tonnes, compared with the same month last year.
LONDON - Federal Express says it will introduce major new initiatives for shippers in Europe.
LONDON - Air France says it has appointed Anne Veyssie as cargo general manager Great Britain and Ireland effective September 16.
ATLANTA - UPS says that a federal court dismissed an antitrust lawsuit brought by General Parcel Service Inc.
COPENHAGEN - Richard Branson says that he had written to a European Union official over what he called unfair action by SAS and would make a formal complaint if necessary.
CHICAGO - Continental Airlines says it will match an air fare sale announced by Trans World Airlines.
